setlist.title: It Must Have Been The Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (3 reviews): The jam coming out of Stranger flowed into Franklin's Tower and was sweet; First set opened with Stranger into Franklin's; Phil's voice was stable on Box, Roses and Masterpiece [18][23][26]
- **Box Of Rain** (2 reviews): Phil was coaxed to the microphone for it and stumbled over lyrics, singing about forgetting them; The crowd went wild as Box Of Rain began [18][20]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's is enjoyable as the band begins extending it [26]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song was stretched out; When Push Comes To Shove featured good Jerry guitar [18]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Show is very well played up to Truckin', where the band finally hit a peak [24]
- **Space** (1 other source): There is a very brief St. Stephen tease near the end of Space [5]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Second-set Other One into Stella Blue was fantastic [23]
- **The Mighty Quinn (Quinn the Eskimo)** (1 review): The Quinn blew the reviewer away [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-03-28.141215.sbd.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 166 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: This source is a little hissier than others from the tour [1]
- **gd1988-03-28.sbd.miller.91233.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1988-03-28.151271.fm.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: FM broadcast; 20 songs; 160 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1988-03-28.144490.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac2496**: source not stated; 20 songs; 162 min [5]
- **gd88-03-28.sbd-matrix.9977.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 155 min; rated 4.23/5 by 13 [7]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds pretty good; Recording described as very tasty; Sound quality rated A+ [20][21][23][28]

## Around the show

- Crowd chanted for Phil; he replied that up front you can't always get what you want, then cheers [21]
- This show closed a run of three nights [21]
- Reviewer attended all three nights; band seemed a bit burnt after the previous night [24]
- Second set looks standard on paper, mostly shorter tunes before drums, but doesn't draw you in at first glance [25]
- Phil was in rare form with his comments to the crowd [27]
- Crowd chanted for Phil; he answered that you can't always get what you want, and Box Of Rain followed [29]
- Reviewer told parents of a visit to Old Dominion University to attend, and met high school friends [29]
- Second night was awesome, with Jerry going nuts at the end of Fire; first night was wacky, less well played [24]
- Reviewer calls it a top 5 show of 1988, much better played than the previous night [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-03-28.141215.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-R90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [1]
- **gd1988-03-28.sbd.miller.91233.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [2]. Also: In-house FM to cassette master to DAT to CD supplies the segment from 7:51 in Space to end; Pitch correction was applied with help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd1988-03-28.151271.fm.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master In-House FM Cassettes; unknown receiver > Sony D5M [3]. Also: Ultramatrix soundboard source patches a brief Walkin' Blues transition gap, 2:27 in Drums and 0:39 in Space [3]
- **gd1988-03-28.144490.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Porter; transferred by Nick Carbonetta and SirMick; source: Sennheiser ME-80s > Sony D-5 > Master Cassette - taped by Stephen Porter [5]
- **gd88-03-28.sbd-matrix.9977.sbeok.shnf**: source: IN House FM>Sony D-5>MC>DAT>CDR [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-03-28 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-03-28-grateful-dead-ticket/) [32]
- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1988-03-27 Hampton Coliseum, Hampton, VA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1988-03-27-hampton-coliseum-hampton-va-usa/) [33]

facts.lineage: The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
facts.source: 2 Nakamichi CM100/CP1s: one on each stack 1 Nakamichi CM300/CP1 straight at stage Nakamichi 550 w/Dolby B in OTS.Maxell XLIIS cassettes. Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes.
